evidence_items.explanation: Across five chatbots, 49.6% of answers were problematic, including 19.6% highly problematic; researchers observed confident presentation even when answers were incorrect. These were misinformation-oriented stress prompts, not a representative sample of patient conversations.

evidence_items.locator: Main results, paragraph preceding Figure 1; Methods, response collection
evidence_items.explanation: Testing on January 9–11 documents consequential errors in a newer consumer health system. Performance varied substantially: semi-urgent cases achieved 93.0% accuracy, and a supplementary set of textbook emergencies had no undertriage.

The 21-model evaluation found substantial differences between reasoning stages, including strong final-diagnosis performance. This limits a blanket reading of medical incompetence but does not negate recurring confident errors.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not estimate the error rate in representative everyday medical chatbot use.
No cited evaluation establishes the accuracy-confidence relationship for every model available on April 21, 2026.
